newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan auto group sees 1996 production flat yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan auto group sees 1996 production flat yr/yr.

text.p: Japanese domestic vehicle output is likely to reach 10 million units in 1996, almost unchanged from the 10.20 million produced last year, the leader of a major Japanese automobile industry group said on Wednesday.

"Domestic vehicle sales in the second half of this year are uncertain yet, but overall output is likely to reach 10 million units this (calendar) year," Yoshifumi Tsuji, chairman of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA), told a news conference.
In 1995, Japan's domestic vehicle production fell 3.4 percent from a year earlier.
Automobile industry officials say Japan needs to maintain domestic vehicle production at a level of around 10 million units per year to secure employment.
Japan's automobile-related industry has 900,000 workers, about 10 percent of Japan's total workforce.

Asked if domestic vehicle sales would gain in the fiscal year ending March 1997, Tsuji said: "Domestic sales from April to September were almost flat against the year-ago level. Sales in the second half are still uncertain."
Concerning monthly sales, he said domestic vehicle sales were expected to mark a year-on-year gain in October and added that sales for October so far had shown a 20 percent gain from a year earlier.
Data for Japan's domestic vehicle sales will be announced on November 1.
